Holzbaurechner / Table

Table calculator

Timber for a solid wood dining table or garden table, from the top to the aprons.

How the table is built

The top is made of 140 mm boards, held together by battens underneath. Four 80 × 80 mm legs are joined by aprons. From 2 m long the calculator uses a 40 mm top so that it does not sag.

Wood moves: fixing the top properly

Solid wood swells and shrinks across the grain as the humidity changes. A wide tabletop can move by several millimetres. That is why the top is fixed with tabletop fasteners or slotted holes that allow this movement. Tops that are screwed down rigidly crack over time.

What size for how many people?

Allow about 60 cm of table length per person. Six people fit at a table 1.80 m long. The usual table height is 75 cm, the width 80 to 100 cm.

Step by step: building the table

  1. Acclimatise the timber: stack the boards flat with spacers for a few days in the room where the table will stand, so the moisture content settles before you cut.
  2. Cut to size: cut the tabletop boards, legs and aprons from the cutting list. Leave the top boards a few centimetres long, so you can trim it cleanly after gluing.
  3. Glue up the top: plane the edges straight, apply glue and clamp the boards, alternating clamps above and below. Scrape off the squeeze-out once it has started to set.
  4. Fit the battens: fix the battens firmly only in the middle, and screw them through slotted holes towards the edges. That lets the top move without cracking.
  5. Build the frame: join the aprons to the legs, traditionally with dowels or mortise and tenon, more simply with metal leg brackets. Measure the diagonals: if both are the same, the frame is square.
  6. Fix the top: use tabletop fasteners or buttons from below on the aprons, never screw straight through.
  7. Finish: sand the top to 180 or 240 grit and oil or varnish it.

Oil or varnish for the tabletop?

Hardwax oil soaks into the wood, brings out the grain and can be touched up locally if it gets scratched. For a dining table it is usually the best choice. Varnish forms a closed film and resists stains better, but can only be repaired by sanding the whole surface. For garden tables in larch or Douglas fir, an exterior oil refreshed every year works well.

Tools you need

A circular saw or plunge saw with a guide rail, a drill driver, several long sash clamps, a square, a sander and wood glue. If you cannot plane the boards yourself, ask your timber merchant to plane them and cut them to size.

Frequently asked questions

Which wood is best for a dining table?
Oak is hard, tough and long-lasting, but much more expensive. Pine and other softwoods are cheap and easy to work, but dent more easily. For garden tables, larch and Douglas fir are a good choice.
How thick should a tabletop be?
For dining tables up to 2 m, 28 to 30 mm is usually enough. Longer tables or soft timber are stiffer at 40 mm.

All timber sections are guide values and do not replace a structural calculation. Carports and patio covers may need planning permission and building regulations approval, and a structural engineer's check depending on where you live.
